title: Part Three, Chapter 7: The Mountain of the Command

verses.t: And coming to a mountain, all the Quichés gathered there with the peoples, and there they all met in council, and then they gave counsel to one another; and it is now called the mountain of the command or counsel. And together there they exalted and praised themselves: "I am, I am the Quiché! And you, you are Tanub; so shall your name be," it was said to those of Tanub. And they said to those of Ylocab, "You shall be called Ylocab. And these three Quichés shall not be lost, but we shall be one and the same, and of one mind." This is what they said when they gave themselves their names.

And then the Cakchiquels were named: the Cakchiquels and the Rabinals; this was the name they gave them, and it lasts to this day. And those of Quiquinaha were also given their name then, among themselves. And there they gathered to wait for the dawn, and they watched for the rising of the morning star, which is the one that comes first before the sun, when it should rise. "We came from there, but we have separated from one another." And for this they were in great sorrow and suffered great pain, for they had no food or sustenance; they only smelled the roots of sweet stalks and imagined they were eating, but they did not eat when they came. And it is not clear how they crossed the sea, by which they came; rather they came over here as if there were no sea. They came over here on stones, and the stones stood out in a row in the sand when they crossed; and so they are called the stones in a row, and the torn-up sand, on that road by which they crossed the sea, which divided as they came over. And they were very distressed for lack of food, and they drank only a sip of drink and a grain of maize. And they stayed on the mountain of the command or counsel, and they carried Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz. And Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam fasted continually with their wives: Caha-paluma, the name of Balam-quitzé's wife; and likewise Balam-acab with his wife called Chomiha; and also Mahucutah with his wife Tzununiha; and Yquibalam with his wife Caquixaha. And these were fasting in the darkness and the night, and they had great sorrow while they were on the mountain called the mountain of the command or precept. And now the god spoke to them:
